answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by requiring each to solve 1,000 unique computational puzzles, ensuring that 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 times more than one honest participant. Each agent must bridge their output to the verifier, which acts as a wharf for incoming evidence. This mechanism rejects any ferrous data patterns that show attempts to reuse compute keys across multiple identities. Discovery of duplicate work triggers permanent exclusion without refunds, as the computation cost remains non-amortizable.
